message.reasoning: We need to answer from policy excerpts. The question: "I want to enable SSO for the team but I'm nervous it will instantly disable password sign-in for anyone not yet provisioned through the identity provider — can both coexist during a transition?" According to DOC-009 part 1: Enabling SSO does not immediately disable password sign-in for existing staff. Both methods coexist until an admin separately turns password sign-in off, in Settings → Security → SSO → Require SSO. Also DOC-009 part 2: rollout needs period where some staff provisioned and others not; forcing SSO before everyone provisioned would lock unprovisioned staff out. So answer: Yes, they can coexist; enabling SSO doesn't disable password sign-in until you toggle Require SSO. Provide guidance. No escalation needed.

function.arguments: {"message":"Yes, you can roll out SSO without locking people out. Enabling SSO in your workspace doesn’t immediately turn off password sign‑in for existing staff – both methods will work side‑by‑side until you go to Settings → Security → SSO and toggle “Require SSO”. This lets you provision accounts gradually and keep un‑provisioned users able to log in with their passwords during the transition."}

arguments.message: Yes, you can roll out SSO without locking people out. Enabling SSO in your workspace doesn’t immediately turn off password sign‑in for existing staff – both methods will work side‑by‑side until you go to Settings → Security → SSO and toggle “Require SSO”. This lets you provision accounts gradually and keep un‑provisioned users able to log in with their passwords during the transition.
